payload.body:
Something can look desirable from the outside and still be wrong for the life you actually want. You may be praised for the path, chosen for the role, or surrounded by people who think the opportunity suits you while privately realizing that the life attached to it does not.

Public approval can make your own values harder to hear. You may stay longer because leaving something admired feels like wasting an opportunity, or keep trying to make a role fit because other people are convinced it suits you.

The challenge is noticing what the recognition is asking you to trade. You accept less autonomy, spend more time, give up creative control, or tolerate terms you would question somewhere else because the visible reward makes the exchange look more reasonable than it feels.

What looks desirable from the outside and what you would actually choose are not always the same thing. Recognition matters most when the life attached to it is still one you want.
